items.title: Sonny Rollins — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: he was one of the first, he was the guy that, sort of...woke that up in me at an early age.

ctx.x: No, I was just going to say Duke Ellington was also a big uh uh, player. I remember my brother coming home, and uh, you know, oh, he was so excited about uh

[scatting melody of I Let A Song Go Out Of My Heart] I Let A Song Go Out Of My Heart, and all this stuff. And uh, so, we liked Duke Ellington, uh...uh, my mother had calypso records, you know. So, I heard calypso records. Um...I heard stride piano records, because in those days we always had a piano, but they had these piano rolls, you know. So, all the pianos had rolls, and these rolls were generally by people like James P. Johnson, you know, piano rolls, and uh, that was ubiquitous. And in those days there were…
What did you like about Fats Waller?
